The "Apollo 13" movie, with the module pilot played by Kevin Bacon as Jack Swigert, portrayed Swigert as unprepared for the flight. However, this was untrue, as Swigert had also long worked on developing the module. The dialogue between ground control and the astronauts was taken nearly verbatim from transcripts and recordings, with the exception of the famous line, "Houston, we have a problem." The actual words spoken by Swigert were, "Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here." Ground control responded by saying, "This is Houston. Say again, please." Jim Lovell then repeated, "Houston, we've had a problem."

One other incorrect dialogue in the film is after the re-entry blackout. In the actual re-entry, the Command Module's transmission was not heard, unlike what was depicted in the movie where Tom Hanks (as Lovell) says, "Hello Houston... this is Odyssey... it's good to see you again."

Moving on to an unrelated topic, in Arthur C. Clarke's "2001: A Space Odyssey," there is a description of a character floating in a space station after experiencing weightlessness. The text reads:

I heard people behind me groan and mutter, praying in their anguish and fear. Then my waist was held by invisible hands and I was raised from the floor; at the height of the roof I was turned slowly parallel with the ground and then released so that I floated, immobile and face downwards, far above the people whose faces I could make out in the half-dark as a grey blur, staring up at me. After I had floated the length and breadth of the building I descended quietly, of my own accord, and landed lightly on the spot from where I had been taken, whereupon I walked directly out of the building without looking back.
